summary: Tested Remember Driver Phone + Forgot PIN Request end-to-end on the preview URL at 390x844, plus the backend. Backend: 15/15 pytest pass when run serially (forgot-pin always gives the same reply, including for unknown or invalid numbers; pin_request_at is set once per 10 min; the per-IP limit returns 200 for requests 1-10 and 429 on the 11th; PUT pin and the one-tap pin/text both clear the request; text-pin 404/401/60s-429; dispatch-phone GET/PUT is admin only (401 without login, 403 for a driver), invalid=400, valid is normalised to +1..., empty clears). Frontend: ?as=driver opens the Driver tab. First sign-in with (519) 555-0101/482913 lands on /driver/drv-1. After sign-out, coming back shows 'Welcome back' with driver-saved-phone and only the PIN field, and PIN + Enter signs in. driver-not-you clears the saved phone, survives a reload, and the phone input comes back. A phone typed in the Admin email field switches to the Driver tab with the phone prefilled and driver-sign-in-notice shown, by tapping the button or pressing Enter. Forgot PIN: no phone shows an error; known and unknown numbers show the same driver-forgot-pin-sent message. Admin /admin/drivers: the FORGOT PIN banner lists drv-2 and drv-3. TEXT NEW PIN on drv-2 gave the toast 'NEW PIN TEXTED TO PRIYA NAIR' (Twilio accepted it) and the request disappeared. Dispatch phone edit: invalid shows a red toast and keeps the input open, valid saves, empty clears. No blocking bugs. Only minor UX and security notes.

minor.issue: Timing leak: a known driver number takes about 0.42s (the admin email and optional Twilio text are awaited inline). Unknown numbers and the cooldown path take about 0.13-0.16s. The generic message can be bypassed by timing to find out which numbers belong to drivers. The per-IP limit (10 per 15 min) reduces the risk. Fix: send the notifications with BackgroundTasks / asyncio.create_task.

ui_bugs.issue: The PIN field is not auto-focused on the Welcome back screen. autoFocus={!!saved} is checked on mount, but `saved` loads asynchronously from AsyncStorage/SecureStore after the field has mounted (document.activeElement was null). Fix: focus a ref once the saved phone loads, or use key={saved ?? 'new'} on the PIN input.

`info` is never cleared. After a 'no phone' error, tapping Forgot PIN again clears the error and the old 'sent' message shows again while the request is still running. forgetPhone() (Not you?) also leaves info/error from the previous driver visible.

issues: The success message (driver-forgot-pin-sent) and the notice use the same cream background as the error box. Only the left border colour changes (green vs red), so success and error look alike at a glance. Consider a green-tinted background.
'ASKED 11:47' shows only the time. Requests stay open with no expiry, so a request from an earlier day looks like today's. Show the date when it is not today.

action_items: LOW: make driver-forgot-pin respond in the same time for known and unknown numbers by sending the admin email and Twilio text in the background.
LOW: auto-focus the PIN field when the saved phone finishes loading (the autoFocus prop has no effect after mount).
LOW: clear `info` when starting a new forgot-PIN request, on validation errors, and in forgetPhone().
OPTIONAL: give the forgot-PIN success message a green-tinted background; show the date on old FORGOT PIN requests.
critical_code_review_comments: The per-IP forgot-pin limit counts every request (record_failure before the lookup), so the 10th request locks the IP and the 11th gets 429. This matches the spec.
The saved phone is stored only after a successful sign-in, and initialPhone (carried from the Admin tab) takes priority over the saved phone. Both are correct.

test_forgot_pin_dispatch_phone.py must be run with -n 0. Under xdist, another worker's module cleanup deletes the pinreq: keys in the middle of the rate-limit test (this was a false failure on the first run).

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows (minor UX notes only)

seed_data_creation: None. Restored afterwards: drv-2 PIN 730516 and drv-3 PIN 264871 (both verified by login), drv-2's original open pin_request_at, drv-3 request cleared, pin_texted_at cleared for drv-2/3, dispatch_phone left unset (it was unset before), db.login_attempts pinreq:* keys deleted.

Each run uses 15 of the per-IP forgot-pin requests, and the test clears the pinreq: keys itself. Twilio accepted the SMS to the fictional drv-2 number (invite='sent'), so the UI toast was 'NEW PIN TEXTED TO PRIYA NAIR' and no PIN was shown. Driver sign-out goes to /driver.
